sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Live-cell staining with anti-Rim antibody on non-permeabilized HEK293 cells confirmed surface expression; no functional assay reported for the tagged PLXDC1 construct itself.
sites.rationale: L5 explicitly states that all constructs—including full-length PLXDC1 (Figure 1H in L3/L4)—carry the Rim epitope tag after the secretion signal at the N-terminus. The native PLXDC1 signal peptide spans residues 1–18 (authoritative landmark), so the tag is placed after residue 18 and before the mature N-terminus at residue 19. No specific residue number is named in the paper, so the position is topology-derived from the single extracellular N-terminus. The tag is 408 residues from the TM boundary, satisfying the ≥3-residue constraint. Full-length PLXDC1 expressed in HEK293 cells with the Rim epitope tag engineered after the secretion signal at the N-terminus (extracellular face); live-cell staining confirmed surface expression of the tagged construct (Figure 1H).

sources.claim: All constructs have the epitope tag engineered after the secretion signal at the N-terminus.

literature_notes: L1 describes a chimeric construct in which the DCC transmembrane domain (not PLXDC1's own TM) is fused to a Rim tag and the PLXDC1 cytoplasmic tail; because the TM domain is heterologous this is not evidence for full-length PLXDC1 surface tagging and was not promoted to a site. L2 describes the AP-signal + Rim-tag construction method applied to the PLXDC1 extracellular domain, which could be a soluble ECD; L3–L5 confirm that the same tag strategy was applied to the full-length membrane-anchored PLXDC1 construct (Figure 1H, live-cell staining). L6 and L7 describe a C-terminal myc tag on full-length PLXDC1 used in co-immunoprecipitation; the C-terminus (residues 448–500) is intracellular per the authoritative topology landmarks, so this tag is not on the extracellular surface and is recorded in other_positions.

literature_other_positions.note: Full-length PLXDC1 carries a C-terminal myc tag used in co-immunoprecipitation; the C-terminus (residues 448–500) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so this tag is not on the extracellular surface.
